messages:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: GitHub Actions + GitHub Packages outage affecting CI/CD pipelines (hotfix builds failing). Severity: P2. Link: https://www.githubstatus.com/ (monitoring).

Jamie (oncall): I'm on it. Seeing failures in eng-releases workflows — checkout step times out, package restore from ghcr.io errors with 503/timeout. Hotfix build for customer-123 blocked.

Sasha (eng-release): Confirmed. Example log: `Error: request to https://api.github.com/repos/redwood/infra/actions failed, status 503` and `npm ERR! 503 GET https://npm.pkg.github.com/@redwood/cli`. Hotfix branch: `hotfix/patch-123` — CI never gets past restore.

Leo (eng-sre): Quick triage: this looks limited to GitHub Actions / Packages — GitHub's status shows degraded service in Actions and Packages. Our cloud infra (GCP) and internal artifact storage are fine. We should plan a mitigation to unblock the hotfix deploys: 1) attempt self-hosted runner fallback, 2) mirror critical packages to S3/npm public if possible, 3) consider manual CI runs on ephemeral VMs.

Mike (eng-infra): I can spin up self-hosted runners in the GCP project and bypass actions' hosted runners for the job steps that need to run locally. Caveat: some workflows rely on `actions/checkout` and other GH-provided actions which still reach GitHub APIs; we'll avoid them by doing a raw `git clone` using an archive URL or pushing the tarball to the runner. Commands I'll try:

```
# on ephemeral runner
git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/redwood/infra.git -b hotfix/patch-123 /tmp/work
cd /tmp/work
./ci/build.sh --skip-gh-checkout
# produce artifact
tar -czf hotfix.tar.gz build/
aws s3 cp hotfix.tar.gz s3://redwood-temp-artifacts/hotfix-1710493200.tar.gz
```

Jamie (oncall): Good. Also package restore is failing for private packages in GH Packages. Short-term workaround: publish critical package tarballs to s3 and update package.json to point to the s3 tarball URL for the hotfix branch. Sasha, can you assemble the patch?

Sasha (eng-release): I'm creating branch `hotfix/github-outage-workaround`. Patch will: 1) replace `@redwood/cli` dependency with "@redwood/cli": "https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-temp-artifacts/redwood-cli-1.2.3.tgz", 2) add `CI_MANUAL_RUN=true` flag to skip steps that require GH-hosted actions. Drafting PR now.

Olivia (customer-support): Customer impact: Customer-123 and a handful of enterprise customers with on-demand hotfixes are blocked from receiving the build. No user-facing API degradation reported for hosted API yet. We should prepare a targeted status update: short explanation + ETA. Suggested message: "We're experiencing an upstream GitHub service outage affecting our CI and deploy pipelines. We've initiated manual mitigations and expect the hotfix to deploy within 1-2 hours."

Tara (product): Please include whether the workaround affects package integrity or telemetry (e.g., different build environment). Need to know if we should pause canary/rollout.

Leo (eng-sre): Recommendation: run canary at 1% behind feature flag and keep close monitoring. If the manual deploy uses a different runner/image, add extra tracing tags `source=manual-runner` to telemetry. I'll add a temporary alert: `deploy.sanity.failures > 0 for 10m` to SRE dashboard.

Mike (eng-infra): Self-hosted runner spin-up logs: `runner-ephemeral-01 registered`, `runner-ephemeral-02 registered`. Running the manual build now. If GH auth to checkout is failing, using `GITHUB_TOKEN` won't help — we'll use direct `git` over HTTPS public clone for the repo and attach the private package tarballs from s3.

Sasha (eng-release): PR pushed: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4827 (hotfix/github-outage-workaround). Build step updated to use `curl -O https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-temp-artifacts/redwood-cli-1.2.3.tgz` then `npm install ./redwood-cli-1.2.3.tgz`. Marking `ci:manual` in commit message.

deploy-bot: Manual deploy command queued by Jamie: `redwoodctl deploy --cluster=dedicated-prod --image=redwood/hotfix:20260315-4827 --tags=canary=1% --reason="github-actions outage workaround"`.

Jamie (oncall): Manual run succeeded on runner-ephemeral-02: build/artifact produced. Artifact uploaded to s3://redwood-temp-artifacts/hotfix-1710493200.tar.gz. Starting canary deploy at 1%.

Olivia (customer-support): Drafted customer note: "We're applying a manual deployment due to a vendor outage with GitHub Actions. The workaround bypasses GitHub Packages by using a temporary artifact store. We expect completion within 60-90 minutes. No data loss. We'll follow up when fully rolled out." Please review.

Sasha (eng-release): Canary reports look clean so far (0 errors, latency within expected). Rolling to 5% after 15m observation window per runbook.

Leo (eng-sre): Observability: added debug tags and a temporary regression alert. CPU/RPS for canary hosts normal. If errors spike, we'll rollback to previous image `redwood/release:stable`.

Tara (product): Approve canary progression to 5% as long as telemetry stays green. Thanks team.

Jamie (oncall): Handoff: I'm oncall for another 30m, then Sasha (eng-release) will take over follow-up and final rollback/rollout decisions. Next steps: 1) keep monitoring GitHub status, 2) finish PR + merge once manual verification passes, 3) publish final customer update.

Mike (eng-infra): Follow-up: I'll add a short playbook to `eng-infra/ops/gh-outage.md` with steps to mount s3 artifacts and run ephemeral runners for quick future outages.

Sasha (eng-release): Merged hotfix branch, manual deploy completed to 5% without error. Marking thread as incident-resolved-for-deploys — still monitoring upstream GitHub status and will revert package.json changes once GH Packages are back. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident note appended: Mitigation — manual builds via self-hosted runners + S3-hosted artifacts. Root cause: GitHub Actions/Packages outage (third-party). Impact: blocked hotfix CI/CD, limited customer impact due to manual workarounds.

Jamie (oncall): Summary for postmortem: cause = third-party outage (GitHub Actions + Packages); mitigation = manual runner + artifact mirror; customer impact = delayed hotfix deploy for a small number of customers ~60–90m; action items: document runbook, consider alternate package mirrors for critical packages, and add a fallback runner script. Assigning follow-ups to Mike and Sasha.

Leo (eng-sre): Logging handoff: I've added timeline notes to the incident ticket and flagged for postmortem. Closing Slack thread for active ops — move follow-ups to the incident PM ticket.

Jamie (oncall): Thanks all — handing over to Sasha.
